messages.text: I’ll read the repository’s design and coding rules, inspect the investigation and current tree, then write the ExecPlan before changing implementation. I’ll keep clear of the two engine files owned by other agents and won’t commit.

The repository confirms the central constraint: catalogs already carry both finalized and unfinalized group records, but the current ranking coordinator buffers all finished outcomes before publishing. I’m tracing how to preserve stable catalog IDs and the existing review journal while publishing partial snapshots, then I’ll encode that boundary in the plan.

The staged refresh database is intentionally separate from the live catalog until publication. I’ll publish immutable catalog snapshots from that staged database as ranking progresses, and merge review events made during the live review into the staged database before the final refresh publishes. That preserves the existing refresh safety boundary while making ready groups usable immediately. I’m recording this and the recovery marker in the required plan now.

The plan is in place. I’m implementing the persistence and engine reporting first, since the UI can only reflect safe ready states after group membership and ranking have been durably associated with catalog IDs. I’ll add tests alongside each layer and avoid the concurrently owned boundary and Flash modules.

The engine now has the explicit completion marker and incremental group storage/reporting path. One integration detail surfaced: the engine currently rejects review-event writes during analysis, and its staged refresh would otherwise replace those decisions at completion. I’m adding a small shared lock so review events can be written to both stores while analysis is active and safely synchronized at final publication.

I’m continuing with implementation and acceptance checks. First I’m checking the current diff and the interrupted-analysis test patch, then I’ll fill the remaining tests and run the requested Rust suites.

The core flow is in place: staged catalogs publish per completion, the app accepts review actions only for finalized captures, and the completion marker gates recovery and Finish. I found the local test helpers already support gated ranking requests; I’m extending those helpers to assert readiness order and split behavior, then adding the UI state checks.

The tests now cover out-of-order group readiness, split placeholders, failure fallback, app progress, and recovery. I’m formatting only files within my ownership; the workspace has unrelated concurrent edits in `flash.rs` and `boundary.rs`, which I’m leaving untouched. Next I’m running the package suite serially against the available X11 display.

The suite stopped before compiling our changes because this image has `libwayland-client.so.0` but lacks its pkg-config development file. I found the prior X11 test setup; I’m adding a temporary `/tmp` pkg-config entry that points at the installed runtime library, keeping all Cargo and source configuration unchanged.

The X11 invocation also needs Iced’s `x11` feature enabled; without it, Winit intentionally refuses to build on Linux. The feature-enabled test command is waiting on Cargo’s shared target lock, likely due another workspace build, so I’m using that time to finish checking the staged refresh/event synchronization and preserving the other agents’ changes.
